BODY MEASUREMENTS
4.1
INTRODUCTION
In order to make a garment, it is essential to take the measurement
of the person for whom
the garment is being made. If the measurements
are not taken properly then the garment
will have an ill-fit. There are some rules of measuring
and many ways of doing it. But we
will first find out why it is necessary to measure correctly, the precautions
to be observed
while taking measurements,
etc.
4.2
OBJECTIVE
After reading this lesson, you will be able to do the following:
•
use the inchtape correctly;
•
use the various methods of measuring;
•
observe precautions
during measuring;
•
take measurements
systematically.
4.3
USING THE INCH-TAPE FOR MEASURING
The tape which is used to take measurements
is known as the "inch-tape". This is generally
made of cloth orplastic.
It has a metal strip of3" at one end andanotherofYz"
at the other
end. The end with the 3" strip is used for measuring lengths and the side with the smaller strip
is used for measuring widths and circumferences.
The tape is marked in inches on one side
and both in centimeter
and inches on the reverse. Every inch is marked in 8 points.

So that precise measurements can be taken. In this way, the measuring tapes can be used
to measure any part of the body for the garment to be made.

4.4
MEASURINGCORRECTLY
The fit of a garment depends upon the cutting and stitching of the garment. The basis of
cutting is measurement because only when proper measurements have been taken can a
gamient be cut properly. Hence, it becomes essential for a beginner to know the various
methods of taking measurements so that a well fitting garment can be prepared. There are
two methods of measuring:
i)
Chest measuring system
il)
Direct measuring system
i)
Chest Measuring
System
In this system the chest measurement forms the basis of all other measurements used for
the drafting.
ii)
Direct Measuring System
In this system, the different parts of the body are precisely measured in order to get a well
fittinggarment.
Observe the following while measuring:
a)
The inch-tape should not be bent or curled at any place.
b)
While measuring circumference, place 2-3 fingers inside, below the tape and the
thumb on the outside.
c)
Use the W' strip end to measure widths and circumferences and the 3" strip side
for lengths.
There are basically three kinds of measures :-
1.
Lengths - full length of the garment, shoulder to waist, length of sleeve, etc. and
for lower garments - the length from waist down, crotch length, etc.
2.
Widths - across shoulders,across
back, etc .
. 3.
Circumferences
- The inch tape is wrapped round the area to be measured-
round chest, round sleeve, trouser bottoms, round knee, hip, round waist, round
neck, etc.

4.5
PRECAUTIONS WHILE TAKING MEASUREMENTS
The following precautions should be observed while measuring anyone:-
1.
Stand to the right hand side ofthe person being measured.
2.
Exercise strict self control as a tailor.
3.
Talk only as much as required.
4.
Be polite and simple in behaviour.
5.
Avoid standing in front ofthe person being measured.
6.
Some people are shy while being measured. Put them at ease by asking about the
design ofthe garment, etc. while measuring them.
7.
Take measurements systematically and sequentially.

8.
Avoid touching the other person unnecessarily.
9.
Be careful to see that the tape does not turn or fold at anyplace
while measuring.
10.
Use the end with the 3" metal strip to measure lengths and the other end to measure
widths and circumferences.

4.6
USE OF 'L' SCALE
This is made ofwood,
plastic or metal. It is shaped like the letter 'L' of English hence it
is called the 'L' scale. It is 24" long on one side and 12" wide on the other side. It is
graduated
in inches. It is generally
used by tailors as it facilitates
their work and makes
it easier. It can be used to mark vertical and horizontal
lines simultaneously.
It is used to
make draftings. Repeated user of the inch-tape can be avoided by using the 'L' scale while
drafting.
The metal'L'
scale is used in factories
for drafting
on boards,
cloth or paper.
4.7
SEQUENCE
OF TAKING MEASUREMENT
Measurements
must always be taken in a sequence.
Be careful to measure
all lengths if
lengths are being measured
or ifwidths
are being measured,
then measure
all widths at

the same time. Taking measurements randomly, that is, one length and then one width and
then back to a length again is not correct. Hence, one should know the sequence in which
measurements must be taken.
1.
ROUND MEASURES
i)
Round Chest
This measure is called 'round bust' for ladies and 'round chest' for men. In order
to take the correct measurement,pass
the tape under the arms, across the back
and hold the ends in front, in center ofthe chest.
Fig 4.2
ii)
Round Waist
This is also a round measure. The place to be measured is the narrow part below
the chest and above the hips.

Round hip
The protruding,
extended part on the backside, is the hip area. The round
measurement of the area is called the round hip. It is called 'hip' for women and
'seat' for men. It is advisable to insert two fingers below the tape while measuring.

iv)
Round neck
This is the round measurement for the neck. The end of tape with the smaller strip
should be used to take this measurement: It is best sto keep one finger inside,
under the tape and the thumb on the outside.
Fig 4.5 Round neck
v)
Knee measurement
The measurement is taken according to the liking ofthe person. This is generally

vi)
Calf
The museu lar portion 0fthe leg below the knee is called the calf This measurement
is taken for well- fitting lower garments
like churidar pyjama, etc.
vii)
Round bottom
This measurement
is taken both for upper and lower body garments.
In the upper
body garments
it is called the round bottom sleeve and in lower body garments
it is called lower round bottom, e.g. in trousers, pajamas,
etc. This measurement
varies with the prevailing
fashion.

WIDTH MEASURES
i)
Shoulders
This is to be taken from the backside. The measurement is from one end ofthe
shoulders to the other.
Fig 4.8 Shoulder measurement
ii)
Across chest
This is to be taken from the front. It is measured at the narrowest part of the chest-
from the middle of arm syce of one side to the other.
3.
LENGTH MEASURES
i)
Sleeve length
The end of the tape is placed at the top of the shoulder and the desired sleeve
length is then measured.

to waist

down to the waist which is the narrow part below
the chest.

iii)
Full length
The full length for upper body garments is taken from the front by placing the end.
of the tape at the base of neck and measuring
up to the desired length of garment.
Fig 4.11 Full length
measurement
iv)
Length
The length is measured
for lower body garments like trousers, etc, by placing the
end of the tape one inch below the navel and measuring
upto the toe. This length
can be varied as desired.

Crotch length
This length is measured from the point where both legs meet and is taken on the
